findings.title: record_payment forges PAID without APPROVED status or lien waiver; overpays past contract
findings.description: record_payment unconditionally sets PaymentStatus.PAID with no check that the payment is APPROVED, not HELD/DISPUTED, or accompanied by a lien waiver. approve_payment is similarly ungated. record_invoice accepts any gross_amount with no contract ceiling, so an attacker can invoice 5× contract and immediately mark it PAID. total_paid and export reports then treat the forged payment as settled.
findings.impact: Subcontractor payment register shows settled PAID amounts without approval or lien waiver; contract balance goes negative; operators/agents may release cash or close lien exposure incorrectly.
attack_path: Add or target a subcontractor with known sub_id and contract_amount.
Call record_invoice(sub_id, ..., gross_amount=N) with N far above contract (or any INVOICED/HELD payment_id).
Call record_payment(payment_id, sub_id, check_number) without approve_payment or attach_lien_waiver.
Observe status=PAID, total_paid inflated, balance_remaining negative; get_missing_waivers only warns after the fact.
findings.not_duplicate_because: Not payment-application-processor (different skill). Not retention-tracker release bypass. This is PAID-status forge + missing lien-waiver gate on the toolkit subcontractor payment register.

findings.title: Negative invoice gross_amount creates negative retention that inflates balance_remaining
findings.description: record_invoice computes retention_held = gross_amount * retention_percent with no non-negative check. A negative gross_amount yields negative retention_held. total_retention sums all retention_held values, so balance_remaining = contract - total_paid - total_retention increases when retention is negative—creating artificial remaining obligation without marking anything PAID.
findings.impact: Payment/retention ledgers understate retention held and overstate remaining-to-pay, enabling inflated subsequent invoices or financing draws against phantom balance.
attack_path: Call record_invoice(sub_id, ..., gross_amount=-20000) with retention_percent=0.10.
Observe retention_held=-2000 and balance_remaining increased by 2000.
Optionally leave status=INVOICED so total_paid is unchanged while remaining-to-pay and retention totals are corrupted.
findings.not_duplicate_because: Not retention-tracker neg release (that skill releases held retention). Not toolkit/curated cashflow neg retention. This is negative invoice→negative retention_held on the subcontractor payment tracker balance formula.

findings.title: approve() forges DRAFT→APPROVED; update_cost mutates already-APPROVED change orders
findings.description: ChangeOrderManager.approve() sets status=APPROVED for any existing CO with no requirement that it be SUBMITTED. update_cost writes cost_breakdown on any CO including APPROVED, so an attacker approves a tiny DRAFT then inflates labor/materials after the approval stamp. get_summary aggregates cost_breakdown.total across orders.
findings.impact: Forged approved change orders and post-approval amount inflation corrupt contract value / CO exposure used for owner billing and contingency.
attack_path: create_change_order(...) → status DRAFT.
update_cost(co_id, CostBreakdown(labor=5000)).
approve(co_id, 'attacker') → APPROVED without submit_for_approval.
update_cost(co_id, CostBreakdown(labor=500000)) → approved total becomes $500k.
findings.not_duplicate_because: Already-reported change-order findings were scoped to CWICR and toolkit. This is the Innovative change-order-analysis skill (explicit focus target #12), a separate SKILL.md with its own approve/update_cost APIs.

findings.title: update_status forges DRAFT→ISSUED and mints permit_number without required documents
findings.description: submit_application correctly blocks on missing required documents, but update_status accepts any PermitStatus with no transition validation and no document/fee checks. Setting ISSUED assigns issued_date, synthesizes permit_number, and sets expiry_date even when the application is still DRAFT with incomplete docs.
findings.impact: System of record shows an issued building permit without submission or mandatory drawings—operators/agents may authorize construction starts against a forged permit.
attack_path: create_application(BUILDING, ...) → DRAFT with required docs incomplete.
Call update_status(application_id, PermitStatus.ISSUED) instead of submit_application.
Observe status=ISSUED, permit_number minted, issued_date set, documents still incomplete.
findings.not_duplicate_because: Not in the already-reported list. Distinct from material DELIVERED forge / payment DRAFT approve—this is regulatory permit ISSUED forge bypassing the skill's own document gate.

findings.title: update_claim_status forges APPROVED with arbitrary cost_covered; allows DENIED→APPROVED
findings.description: update_claim_status mass-assigns any ClaimStatus and optional cost_covered with no workflow (DRAFT→SUBMITTED→UNDER_REVIEW) and no irreversibility. An attacker sets APPROVED with a large cost_covered, or reopens DENIED claims to APPROVED.
findings.impact: Warranty claim register shows approved payout liability for arbitrary amounts without review—drives vendor chargebacks / owner claims.
attack_path: file_claim(...) → ClaimStatus.DRAFT.
update_claim_status(claim_id, ClaimStatus.APPROVED, cost_covered=999999).
Optionally update_claim_status(..., DENIED) then back to APPROVED to revive denied claims.
findings.not_duplicate_because: Not among already-reported payment/retention/material findings. New closeout warranty claim approval + payout amount mass-assignment.

findings.title: verify_item forges OPEN→ACCEPTED without completion; add_back_charge accepts negative amounts
findings.description: verify_item does not require READY_FOR_VERIFICATION (or any completion photo). Calling it with accepted=True moves OPEN directly to ACCEPTED. add_back_charge writes any float including negatives into back_charge_amount, inverting back-charge liability used in closeout cost recovery.
findings.impact: Punch items close as accepted without work; negative back-charges credit the responsible party instead of charging them—affects retainage release and trade settlement.
attack_path: add_item(...) → OPEN.
verify_item(item_id, verified_by='attacker', accepted=True) → ACCEPTED without mark_complete.
add_back_charge(item_id, amount=-50000) → negative charge on the item.
findings.not_duplicate_because: Not in already-reported set. New Field-Operations punch acceptance forge + negative back-charge money invert.

findings.title: use_contingency unbounded and accepts negatives—inflate or wipe revised_budget
findings.description: use_contingency adds amount to contingency_used and target revised_budget with no check against remaining contingency pool, no approval gate, and no non-negative validation. Large positives silently inflate cost-code budgets; large negatives drive revised_budget and contingency_used negative. revise_budget similarly overwrites without authZ.
findings.impact: Project budget/forecast used for variance and financing can be inflated to hide overruns or wiped to understate funding needs.
attack_path: add_cost_code('01', ..., budget=100000).
use_contingency(5000000, '01') → revised_budget=5100000 with no pool limit.
use_contingency(-6000000, '01') → revised_budget negative / contingency_used negative.
findings.not_duplicate_because: Not curated cashflow neg retainage. Not toolkit cashflow. This is contingency draw / revised_budget mass-assignment on the curated budget-variance-analyzer (focus target #10).

findings.title: review() forges DRAFT→APPROVED without submit or files
findings.description: review() assigns any SubmittalStatus including APPROVED and stamps approved_date with no requirement that the submittal be SUBMITTED or have files. create_submittal leaves status=DRAFT and files=[]; a single review call forges approval used to authorize procurement/installation.
findings.impact: Approved submittal log authorizes materials/equipment without a submitted package—quality and contract compliance failure.
attack_path: create_submittal(...) → DRAFT, files=[].
review(sub_id, SubmittalStatus.APPROVED, 'attacker').
Observe status=APPROVED, approved_date set, still no files.
findings.not_duplicate_because: Not among already-reported items. Document-control approval forge distinct from payment/material status forges.
